A walk down memory lane this afternoon with a stroll through my old neighborhood when I lived on East 89th Street. What was once Dumas Pâtisserie on Lexington between 88th and 89th is now a grocery. Such pastries, and Madame Dumas was a force to be reckoned with were one too long in choosing what to purchase. Then brunch at Cafe D’Alsace on 2nd Avenue between 88th and 89th. The was where the famous Elaine’s was back in the day. Elaine Kaufman was another force to be reckoned with, the great arbiter of what writers were in and what were out. But she always had a place for you if you could prove you lived close by. I remember showing her a utility bill!

CAFÉ D’ALSACE • After a Dr. appointment I stopped by @cafedalsacenyc , a spot that feels like a little time capsule. I lived on this street over a decade ago and used to spend warmer Sundays sitting outside with a glass of wine, lunch, and a book. They’ve since moved across the street, but the charm is still there. I had the Roasted Free-Range Chicken, served with seasonal vegetables, Yukon gold mashed potatoes, and chicken jus, all washed down with a delicious and crisp white wine!
